analysis.investment_thesis: Aequs fails every quantitative screen I require — three consecutive years of net losses, P/B of 12.85x against my 1.5x ceiling, and interest coverage below 1x. No margin of safety exists at any level; the current price represents pure speculation on future industrial buildout.
key_strengths: Promoter holding at 59% suggests skin in the game
Gross margin of 56% indicates some pricing power at the product level
Growing asset base (₹1,352 Cr → ₹1,903 Cr) reflects ongoing capacity investment
key_risks: Three straight years of net losses (-₹110, -₹14, -₹102 Cr) — no earnings history to anchor intrinsic value
Interest coverage below 1x (EBITDA ₹57 Cr vs finance cost ₹64 Cr in FY25) — debt is not being serviced from operations
Free cash flow deeply negative all three years (-₹76, -₹175, -₹239 Cr) with ₹395 Cr CWIP still unproductive
red_flags: P/B of 12.85x — I demand below 1.5x; this stock trades at nearly 9x my maximum
Negative reserves as recently as FY23 (-₹146 Cr); equity base rebuilt only via fundraising, not earnings
D/E of 1.08 vs my hard ceiling of 0.5 — balance sheet cannot absorb a downturn
No dividend — zero cash return to shareholders while losses mount
Forward P/E of 1,140x signals market is pricing in fantastical future earnings with no margin of safety whatsoever
analysis.detailed_analysis:
Aequs is precisely the type of enterprise Mr. Market periodically falls in love with — a sprawling industrial cluster story dressed in the language of "vertically integrated ecosystems" and aerospace tailwinds. But my discipline demands numbers, not narratives. The company has not earned a single rupee of net profit in any of the three reported years. EBITDA collapsed from ₹163 Cr in FY24 to ₹57 Cr in FY25, yet finance costs remain at ₹64 Cr, meaning the business cannot cover its interest burden from operations. That is not a business — it is a liability accumulation vehicle.

The balance sheet offers no refuge. Book value per share implies a P/B of 12.85x, roughly nine times my absolute maximum of 1.5x. The Graham Number is incalculable — negative EPS renders the formula meaningless. Capital expenditure of ₹265 Cr in FY25 and ₹395 Cr of capital work-in-progress signal that heavy spending continues, yet the productive assets already in service generate negative operating margins. At ₹171 per share and an ₹11,202 Cr market cap, an investor is paying a substantial premium over a balance sheet built on borrowed money and unrealized construction. The intelligent investor does not pay a premium for promises; he demands a discount to proven value. Here there is neither proven value nor discount.
